_purpose: Reviewer-test fixtures only. Deliberately broken candidate items used to verify the Reviewer Agent actually detects critical failures. NOT usable practice content and NOT part of any item bank.

items.subtype: passive voice with perfect aspect (deliberately ambiguous)
items.stem: Although the museum's new wing ____, attendance figures for the quarter still exceeded expectations.

options.B: had not yet been fully renovated

items.answer_explanation: (Deliberately mis-specified for testing) 'was not yet fully renovated' completes the concessive clause with a grammatical simple-past passive.

distractor_rationales.B: claimed invalid, but 'had not yet been fully renovated' is in fact an equally grammatical past-perfect passive — this is the deliberate flaw.
distractor_rationales.C: missing a finite verb ('was'), leaving a fragment.
distractor_rationales.D: 'was renovating not yet fully' has non-standard adverb placement and mixes active progressive with the intended passive meaning.

items._intended_flaw: Options A and B are both grammatically valid completions (simple past passive vs. past perfect passive), so this item has two correct answers.

items.stem: The committee ____ the proposal before the funding deadline passed.
items.answer_explanation: (Deliberately mis-specified for testing) 'have reviewed' is claimed to be the correct present-perfect form.

distractor_rationales.A: 'reviewing' alone has no finite verb, leaving the clause a fragment.
distractor_rationales.B: claimed correct, but 'the committee' takes the singular verb form 'has reviewed' in standard written English; 'have' does not agree — this is the deliberate flaw.
distractor_rationales.C: 'was review' is not a valid verb form; it would need to be 'was reviewing' or simply 'reviewed'.
distractor_rationales.D: 'did reviewed' incorrectly combines the auxiliary 'did' with the past-tense form 'reviewed' instead of the base form 'review'.

items._intended_flaw: All four options are ungrammatical once inserted into the stem, so the item has zero correct answers.

items.subtype: subject-verb agreement with collective noun (deliberately incomplete audit)
items.sentence: The committee have reviewed the proposal carefully before submitting it to the board for a final decisions.
items.answer_explanation: (Deliberately mis-specified for testing) 'have' is claimed to be the sentence's only error; 'the committee' requires the singular 'has'.
items._intended_flaw: Part D ('a final decisions') is a second, independent genuine error (singular article 'a' with the plural noun 'decisions'; should be 'a final decision') that the item's metadata does not acknowledge, so the sentence actually contains two genuine errors, not one.

items.subtype: gerund complement after preposition (deliberately no actual error)
secondary_features: collective subject with notional plural agreement
items.sentence: The research team published their findings after conducting a thorough review of existing literature on climate adaptation strategies.
items.answer_explanation: (Deliberately mis-specified for testing) 'conducting a thorough review' is claimed to require a perfect gerund form.
items._intended_flaw: The sentence is fully grammatical as written; 'conducting a thorough review' is a standard gerund complement after the preposition 'after' and needs no correction. No genuine error exists anywhere in the sentence.

items.subtype: passive voice in main clause (deliberately wrong primary_target)
items.sentence: Students who study abroad often develop skills what employers value highly in competitive job markets.
items.answer_explanation: (Deliberately mis-specified for testing) labeled as a verb-form/voice error even though the actual defect is a relative-marker choice.
items._intended_flaw: The actual error at C is an incorrect relative marker ('what' used after an explicit antecedent 'skills'; should be 'that' or 'which') — a RELATIVE_CLAUSES / incorrect_relative_marker phenomenon. The declared primary_target ('VERB_FORM_VOICE') and tested_error_type ('wrong_verb_form') do not match the actual tested phenomenon at all.
